title: Onramp playtest snapshot — quickstarts & SDK handoff
content:
Context:
This doc is a fast snapshot from the 10/05 DevEx playtest check-in. We ran the first half-day of onramp playtests with 6 pilot customers (internal + partner accounts). Focus: quickstarts, sample apps, and the SDK onboarding flow.

Goals for the session:
- Validate that Quickstart-Node and Quickstart-Python work from a cold machine (fresh env)
- Verify samples repo builds and demo pages load in <= 3s for dev machines
- Surface any friction that blocks first-API-call success for new users
- Exercise telemetry to ensure no double-counting of preview tokens

What happened (high level):
- 5/6 seats completed first API call within 7 minutes. One seat failed due to missing env var in bash profile on Windows (Cygwin path issue).
- Quickstart-Node: streaming example had token chunk boundaries that broke our simple newline-joiner demo; caused garbled assistant messages in the browser.
- Quickstart-Python: worked end-to-end but crash observed when running with Python 3.9 on M1 (arm64 wheel fallback triggered an edge path in native client).
- Samples web app: first-page assets loaded slowly because the sample downloads the demo model weights (bad default). We need to switch to lightweight metadata-only fetch for the public demo.
- Telemetry: billing events were emitted for the same request twice in the client integration path (SDK emitted + browser instrumentation). Root cause appears to be both the SDK client and the sample wrapper emitting events.

Notes / raw snippets from playtest feedback:
- "Docs assume bash; Windows users get lost at step 2" — participant
- "Streaming piece is neat but the demo code is fragile when chunks split tokens" — internal engineer
- "I had to pip uninstall 'redwood-sdk' and reinstall via wheel to avoid crash" — partner dev

Blocking issues to address (short list):
1) Env var discovery for quickstarts: we should detect common patterns on Windows and surface a clear message. (owner: @diego-m) -> JIRA-INFR-4321
2) Streaming reassembly: improve demo helper to rejoin chunked deltas robustly and include fallback for corrupted sequences. (owner: @rina-k) -> create SDK PR and add unit tests
3) Python arm64 crash: coordinate with release-eng to ensure wheel availability for 3.9/3.10 on mac M1. (owner: @elliot-p)
4) Telemetry duplication: add a single source-of-truth switch in samples wrapper to disable SDK automatic telemetry when wrapper instrumentation is enabled. (owner: @samir-j) -> JIRA-DEVEXP-987
5) Samples asset policy: change demo to fetch model metadata (no weights) and show a "Try in your account" CTA that downloads small payload. (owner: @maya-c)

Action items (with ETA):
- Quick fix (24–48h): Modify quickstart scripts to detect Windows and print explicit instructions; do not rely on profile sourcing. Add a one-liner to set REDWOOD_API_KEY. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2389) — owner: Diego — target: 2026-10-07
- Streaming helper (this sprint): Implement resilient chunk joiner + unit tests; add example with token boundaries explicitly handled. (branch: feat/stream-rejoin) — owner: Rina — target: 2026-10-13
- Python wheel rollout (1 week): Release arm64 wheels for supported Python versions and document version matrix. (task: release-eng coordination) — owner: Elliot — target: 2026-10-12
- Telemetry opt-out flag (48h): Add env REDWOOD_SAMPLES_TELEMETRY=0 default for sample wrappers; update docs and issue warning in console if both telemetry producers enabled. — owner: Samir — target: 2026-10-07
- Samples demo change (this sprint): Replace heavy asset fetch with metadata-only flow + local mock weights for offline dev. — owner: Maya — target: 2026-10-13

Decisions and tradeoffs (agreed in meeting):
- Do NOT ship an auto-download of model weights for public demos — security and bandwidth risk. We'll keep a "download demo weights" opt-in flow.
- Keep telemetry in SDK by default; samples wrappers should explicitly opt-in to emit telemetry to avoid surprises.
- Prioritize Windows onboarding and streaming reassembly above cosmetic doc rewrites.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want the quickstart to attempt automated env var injection (i.e., suggest adding to .bashrc) or only display one-liners? Opinions split — leaning towards only display and explain. (Follow-up owner: Maya)
- Should the streaming helper live in SDK core or samples helpers? Performance and maintenance argue for SDK core, but we need to keep SDK surface minimal. (Follow-up owner: Rina)
- What sampling rate for telemetry in samples is safe to show for public demos? Need legal/product input. (Follow-up owner: Samir)

Observability notes:
- Added a temporary trace tag playtest:onramp-2026-10-05 for product and infra teams to filter traffic.
- Captured one example request-id with duplicated billing events -> trace link attached to JIRA-INFR-4321.

'Notes to self' and quick reminders (informal):
- Add a checkbox into the quickstart README: "Did you set REDWOOD_API_KEY?" with 1-click copy shell command.
- Update samples README with browser compatibility matrix (Edge/Chrome/Safari mobile caveats).
- Consider a "first-run" smoke test that runs on CI for samples repo and fails fast if first API call times out >15s.

Sample pseudo-fallback (to add in docs):
If streaming message appears garbled, fall back to non-streaming call:
  try:
    resp = client.chat.stream(...)
  except StreamParseError:
    resp = client.chat.create(...)
    // show a toaster: "Streaming failed — falling back to standard response"

Meeting artifacts + links:
- Playtest recording: internal drive link (attached to Confluence page)
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2389 (quickstart fix), github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/404 (telemetry opt-out)
- JIRA: JIRA-DEVEXP-987 (telemetry dupe), JIRA-INFR-4321 (env var / windows), SDK-1234 (streaming rejoin)

Next steps / next meeting:
- Quick triage sync Monday 10/07 10:30 PT to confirm quick fixes merged; invite release-eng for wheel plan.
- Full playtest retrospective 10/14 to review metrics and customer feedback (invite partner reps).

If you're reading this and want to be added to the playtest rotation, ping me (Maya) with an email and GitHub handle.

-- end of snapshot (raw, messy as the drive likes it)
